title: A thicker conducting wall
hook: Change wall thickness and predict conducted heat rate.
misconception: conducted heat rate doubles when wall thickness doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply Q̇ = kAΔT/L to compare conducted heat rate when wall thickness changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With steady one-dimensional conduction with fixed area conductivity and temperature difference, Q̇ = kAΔT/L. When wall thickness doubles, conducted heat rate becomes ½ times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model Q̇ = kAΔT/L; scaling exponent -1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider steady one-dimensional conduction with fixed area conductivity and temperature difference, with a nonzero initial result. If wall thickness triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on conducted heat rate?
recall.why: Apply Q̇ = kAΔT/L under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 1/3.
